API contracts and source attribution for the game

Unit 1 · Week 9 · Lesson 1 · Suggested 55-minute plan; adjust to local timing.

Prepare: Open the current Year 11 project brief, project-workbook.md, project-milestones.csv, project-test-log.csv and the selected scenario starter in project-pack.zip. Check the four S01 preparation exits first. Use the shared FR/NFR contract at https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/assessments/games/year11-requirements.md . Keep school-issued support, assessment and submission conditions visible. Use a disposable local folder, synthetic labels, primitive shapes and permitted static assets. Suggested times are untrialled; record actual completion/support and re-plan openly if needed.

Suggested answers are teacher guidance, not extra assessment tasks. These notes are public.

Suggested time: 2 minutes

Instructional strategy: Learning intention

This is the allocated API/attribution theory lesson between project workshops, not an extra workshop. Use workbook sections3 and7. 2. Retrieve a function contract

Suggested time: 5 minutes

Instructional strategy: Individual retrieval and paired explanation

Use one learner-owned function interface, then compare with a documented library call. APIs include local libraries; they do not always need a web service, account or key. Distinguish consulting a reference from copying a code example. Current chapter: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#design . 3. Read the documented operation

Suggested time: 6 minutes

Instructional strategy: Documentation comparison

Use official pygame.Rect.colliderect, pygame.time.Clock.tick and Python open documentation. colliderect expects a rectangle-like value and returns a Boolean using strict edge overlap. tick(60) returns elapsed milliseconds and limits a target rate; it does not prove fixed FPS or responsiveness. open returns a file object or raises an error; append changes persistent storage. 4. Predict an API result before running

Suggested time: 10 minutes

Instructional strategy: Predict–run–investigate

Use this separate practice snippet in a disposable editor, not as an assessed game solution. First call False: player right edge equals station left edge. Moving1 gives True. Learners should identify returned values and document the assumption that the y ranges overlap. Cite the Pygame Rect documentation. 5. Build a source entry you can verify

Suggested time: 10 minutes

Instructional strategy: Worked log and guided review

Model a consultation entry for the Rect API. If reusing this original teaching snippet, identify CS ATAR and the MIT code notice. Record AI/static assets with tool/source/date and relevant conditions; do not assume generated work has no third-party rights. Asset permission does not settle code-assistance permission. 6. Investigate one interface independently

Suggested time: 12 minutes

Instructional strategy: Independent documentation task

Do not copy an entire documentation page. Identify what the operation does not validate for your game, such as once-only collection or the final score range. Explain how a missing history file or failed write must be handled by the learner’s stated policy. Teacher chooses permitted sources/assistance conditions. 7. Does credit settle permission?

Suggested time: 5 minutes

Instructional strategy: Hinge question with reasons

A. Attribution and permission are separate. Seek an approved licensed alternative or teacher guidance when terms are unclear.
